# Rust SDK 0.1.2 supported-contract testnet verification

Date: 2026-07-31 UTC

Reference JavaScript package: `tbc-contract` 1.6.5.

Rust implementation commits: `08586a3`, `2f014b8`, `423c190`, and `94b9748`.

Network/API: TBC testnet, `https://api.tbcdev.org/api/tbc/`.

## Result

- 52 transactions were accepted, returned by the testnet API, and matched their locally calculated txids.
- Every accepted transaction was fetched again with JavaScript 1.6.5 tooling. Every referenced parent output was fetched independently and used to recompute the paid fee.
- Every paid fee is at least `max(80, ceil(serialized_bytes * 80 / 1000))` satoshis.
- One deliberately retained failed diagnostic attempt exposed a StableCoin OrderBook FT-version bug. It was not retried. The corrected Rust transaction is byte-for-byte compatible with the JavaScript 1.6.5 transaction and was accepted under a new txid.

The verified Rust 0.1.2 scope is Base/P2PKH, FT, NFT, StableCoin, and the TBC/FT OrderBook. Pool, MultiSig, HTLC, PiggyBank, and unreleased token-token OrderBook behavior are outside the Rust SDK's supported scope and were not claimed as verified.

## Retained failed diagnostic

The first locally constructed StableCoin OrderBook match had txid `b21d1c85be9c6d78f3b8191afeb6cc187afd63f49f3cf35943f3b683fe8ca7ab`. The testnet node rejected its single broadcast attempt with:

`mandatory-script-verify-flag-failed (Invalid OP_SPLIT range)`

The transaction was not accepted and was not retried. JavaScript's script engine reproduced the failure at input 1 with `SCRIPT_ERR_INVALID_SPLIT_RANGE`. The cause was Rust treating the 2012-byte StableCoin FT code as v2 without inspecting its v3 fill marker, which omitted the contract-input-index `OP_0` immediately before the coin-mode `OP_1`. Commit `94b9748` fixes the classification and adds a real StableCoin-code regression fixture. The corrected Rust transaction passed all four inputs in the JavaScript 1.6.5 script engine and then passed the real testnet broadcast above.
